methodology: Every factual claim on this site is backed by an official government source, statute, regulation, or court rule. Claims in progress are marked pending. This registry is updated as sources change.

sources.claim: Veterans Crisis Line is reachable by calling 988, then pressing 1.

sources.source_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

sources.claim: VA provides mental health and substance use treatment services for enrolled veterans.
VA Community Care under the MISSION Act can authorize care from community providers.
Substance use history alone does not automatically bar VA disability compensation; the disability must still be service-connected under 38 C.F.R.  3.301.
Many states and counties operate Veterans Treatment Courts. Specific programs vary by jurisdiction.
sources.source_name: Local court or Veterans Service Organization

sources.claim: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) is a monthly benefit for surviving spouses and children when a veteran's death resulted from a service-connected condition.
The Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) is a DoD annuity for survivors of military retirees.
sources.source_name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service / DoD Military Pay

sources.claim: CHAMPVA provides health coverage for eligible survivors who cannot use TRICARE.
The Fry Scholarship provides Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to children and spouses of service members who died in the line of duty after September 10, 2001.
Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA, Chapter 35) provides education benefits to dependents of veterans with certain service-connected disabilities or deaths.
Surviving spouses may have options regarding an existing VA-guaranteed home loan.
VA-accredited representatives and Veterans Service Organizations can help survivors file claims.
